subtopics.title: Two Norths and the Angle Between Them

questions.question: True north is the direction to:
options: The geographic North Pole, where the lines of longitude converge
The top edge of any photograph
The magnetic pole in the Earth's core

questions.question: Magnetic declination is:
options: The speed at which a compass needle spins
The angle between true north and magnetic north
The distance between the two poles
The error in a map's scale

questions.question: The declination note in a topographic sheet's margin supplies:
options: The map's scale and contour interval
The declination in a stated year, the mean annual change, and the direction of that change
The bearing of the nearest town

questions.question: How many minutes of arc make one degree?
A sheet gives its declination for 2018 and the question asks for 2026. The year difference to use is:
options: Whatever year the map was printed

questions.question: With a mean annual change of 4 minutes over 8 years, the total change is:
The declination is 17°53' west of true north and the change is 32 minutes westward. You must:
options: Add, because a westward drift widens an already westerly angle
Convert to degrees only and round off

questions.question: 17 degrees 85 minutes must be rewritten before it becomes a final answer. The correct form is:
options: 18 degrees 25 minutes, because sixty minutes carry into one degree

questions.question: The iron rule of the area calculation is:
options: Convert each measured distance to real ground units first, and only then multiply
Multiply the map centimetres first, then convert the square centimetres
Estimate the area by eye before measuring

questions.question: On an orthophoto at 1:10 000, a measured length of 4,2 cm represents:
With converted sides of 420 m and 250 m, the area of the block is:
On a 1:50 000 topographic sheet, a block of 5 cm by 4 cm has an area of:
options: 5 square kilometres, from 2,5 km times 2 km

subtopics.title: Marks, Traps and the Answer Line

questions.question: The three-line skeleton that collects the marks in both calculations is:
options: The given values, the operation, and the answer with its unit and direction
A sketch, a paragraph, a conclusion

questions.question: An answer of 17 degrees 85 minutes west loses a mark because:
options: Sixty or more minutes must carry into degrees before the answer line

questions.question: Which is a named AREA trap?
options: Multiplying the paper centimetres first and converting the square centimetres afterwards

questions.question: The declination year count must start from:
options: The year the map was first surveyed
The year printed in the margin's declination note

subtopics.title: The Compass That Tells a Small Lie

questions.question: In the story of the compass's lie, the size of the lie is:
options: The magnetic declination — the wedge of angle between the two norths
The distance to the North Pole

questions.question: The wedge grows a few minutes wider every year because:
options: The magnetic pole drifts as the Earth's molten core churns
The geographic pole moves with the seasons

questions.question: To walk a direction taken off the map, the translation sentence is:
options: True bearing equals magnetic bearing plus declination
Magnetic bearing equals true bearing minus the map scale
Magnetic bearing equals true bearing plus the declination, for a declination lying west

questions.question: Minutes of angle work like minutes on a clock because:
options: Both pass at the same speed
Angles are read off a wristwatch
Sixty of them roll over into one whole — one hour on the clock, one degree on the map

questions.question: Eight years of growth at 4 minutes per year adds:
53 minutes plus 32 minutes gives 85 minutes, which rolls over to:
options: 1 degree 25 minutes, carried into the degrees column

subtopics.title: The Rugby Field in Your Answer Book

questions.question: The tiling order of operations for a map area question is:
options: Convert the length, convert the breadth, then multiply
Add the two sides and double the total

questions.question: Un-shrinking 2,5 cm on a 1:10 000 orthophoto gives:
Using a rugby field of about 7 000 square metres, a block of 105 000 square metres is roughly:
options: Fifteen rugby fields — a sensible size for a demarcated orthophoto block
The size of a small province

questions.question: Multiplying 4,2 by 2,5 in centimetres first fails because:
options: The numbers are too small to multiply
The answer would be too accurate
The shrinking applied to each side separately, so each side must be un-shrunk separately before multiplying
